pool.text: Diego López V de Haro founded Bilbao with a municipal charter
María Díaz I de Haro extended commercial privileges with a new charter
John I of Castile named Bilbao a free port
Church of Saint Anthony the Great was enshrined
Queen Isabella I swore fealty to the fueros of Biscay in Bilbao
Consulate of the Sea of Bilbao was created by royal order
Bilbao suffered its first bombing by Nationalist aircraft
Strike at Euskalduna shipyard marked first social movement under Franco
First commercial flight departed from Bilbao's local airport
Bilbao Airport opened to the public with a regular flight to Madrid.
First International Festival of Ibero‑American and Filipino Documentary Film held in Bilbao.
Separatist organization ETA was created in Bilbao
University of Bilbao, the first public university, was established
Petronor, a large oil company, founded in Bilbao.
University of Bilbao established, later becoming University of the Basque Country.
Big Week (Aste Nagusia) began annual nine‑day celebration of the city.
Statute of Autonomy approved, Vitoria‑Gasteiz became Basque government seat
City hall took over organization of Big Week, staging events at Arriaga Theatre.
Aste Nagusia floods overflowed estuary, killing two and causing massive damage
Basque‑speaking population represented about 28 % of Bilbao’s total residents.
